EMT fault

EMT fault inserts a switchable low-impedance path at an internal node of a composed EMT branch model. Its algebraic equations preserve the series voltage path and split the through current from the selected fault current.

Typical use

  • Insert it inside an EMT line or other explicitly composed branch model.

  • Select a phase mask consistent with the requested fault topology.

  • Keep all resistance and conductance settings on the parent EMT per-unit base.

The EMT fault is an internal branch-composition block for inserting a switchable low-impedance path at a three-phase EMT node. It is available from the dynamic editor library under Faults only while the editor is in EMT mode. It is not an RMS model and it is not mapped directly to a network device; it must be wired inside a parent EMT branch model, such as a line composition.

Supported topologies

Topology

Required phases

Electrical representation

LG

Exactly one of A, B or C

Selected phase to ground through fault_rg

LL

Exactly two phases

One phase-to-phase path through fault_r

LLG

Exactly two phases

Each phase to a common node through fault_r, then the node to ground through fault_rg

LLL

A, B and C

Three equal paths through fault_r to one floating common node

LLLG

A, B and C

Each phase independently to ground through fault_rg

An invalid phase/topology combination is rejected when the template is built.

Control and parameters

Setting

Meaning

Units/default

initial_closed

Initial value of fault_closed_mode

False

fault_resistance

Closed phase-path resistance R_f

0.01 p.u.

ground_resistance

Closed ground-path resistance R_g

0.01 p.u.

open_conductance

Leakage conductance while open

1e-8 p.u.

signal_controlled

Adds the fault_cmd input and sampled mode update

False

command_threshold

Fault closes when fault_cmd >= threshold

0.5

fault_time_constant

Saved compatibility parameter; not used by the present algebraic model

1e-4 s

Resistances and the compatibility time constant must be finite and positive; the open conductance must be finite and non-negative.

When signal control is disabled, events may change fault_closed_mode directly. When it is enabled, the procedural logic samples fault_cmd and writes the mode according to command_threshold.

Placement side

FromSide and ToSide describe where the user intends to place the fault in a composed branch. The setting is retained in the internal editor projection and is restored after saving and reopening. It does not automatically discover or rewire a neighbouring line block: the outer and inner ports remain explicit, so the parent model author controls the actual connection.

The internal diagram mirrors the selected topology, including the series port path, phase-to-phase link, floating common node, or grounded common node as applicable.
